idiom_name: explicit context struct passed through the call chain (no ambient scope in C)
implementation_notes: C has no component tree and no ambient scope: the only language-level carrier is thread storage duration (_Thread_local, C11, spelled thread_local via <threads.h>), which is process/thread-wide, cannot be nested or overridden per call subtree, and gives no change notification. A real context object therefore has to be passed explicitly - struct app_ctx *ctx as a parameter, the convention used by C APIs such as lua_State - which is precisely the threading this pattern exists to remove. Keep _Thread_local for genuinely process-wide services initialised once at start-up, and never as a general carrier of request state.
pitfalls: Thread-local carriers outlive the request that set them: worker threads in a pool keep the previous value until it is explicitly cleared, so request state leaks into the next job.
A global registry initialised at start-up is the tempting shortcut, but it couples every module to one mutable object and needs atomics or a mutex to be safe under threads.
A block-scope _Thread_local declaration must be combined with static or extern (linkage rules), which is an easy way to write code that silently gets static storage instead.
alternative: Pass an explicit context struct to every function that needs it (classic dependency injection), or use _Thread_local only for process-wide services that are initialised once at start-up and cleared on demand.
